transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-23
Time: 11:30 AM PDT / 18:30 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Priya Nair (Redwood AE), Diego Santos (SE), Noah Patel (CSM); Aisha Rahman (Horizon, Head of Platform), Tom Baker (Security Arch), Sofia Lin (DevOps), Kenji Watanabe (PM)

Auto Summary (auto-generated): Weekly compliance sprint checkin for Horizon Data Systems POC. Main threads: SSO progress, audit log format/retention, SOC2 evidence needs, and quick results/latency snapshot.

---
[00:00] Priya Nair: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check — is this still a good time?
[00:10] Aisha Rahman: Yep, we are good. we have Tom and Sofia on the call to cover security and infra. Kenji might drop in late.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Awesome. I'll kick off with a 2 minute recap of where we are in the pilot, then Diego will run through the audit log ingestion examples and we can move into SSO and retention.
[00:28] Diego Santos: Hi all. quick note, I pulled a few of the example logs you sent last week and tried ingesting them into our parser. noticed some field name variance — user_id vs uid, event_ts vs timestamp. nothing major but it affects the mapping step.
[00:45] Tom Baker: yeah that was our worry. our logging pipeline has a few backwards-compatible shim layers. we can produce an export with normalized fields but need to confirm what PII or IP we should mask out.
[00:58] Sofia Lin: for the POC we prefer minimal masking, but if SOC2 evidence is required we'll need to show anonymized artifacts. we're leaning towards redacting ip and email, keep user action types.
[01:15] Diego Santos: totally makes sense. we can show both: raw ingestion with internal masking rules and an anonymized sample for compliance. I'll prepare a short demo to show how the mapper transforms fields.
[01:30] Priya Nair: Great. Tom, are you able to provide a small sample set — say 7 days — preferably already anonymized or with a mapping note?
[01:40] Tom Baker: yes we can do that. we'll scrub PII but keep event structure. i'll aim to drop that into the shared S3 link by monday.
[01:48] Priya Nair: Perfect. Next — SSO. where are we on the SAML metadata exchange?
[01:57] Aisha Rahman: We had an issue with our IdP; the certificate rotated and our SAML metadata timed out. our security team is fixing it but we should be able to complete the exchange tomorrow.
[02:08] Diego Santos: Once we have the metadata we can spin up a test SP and run an end-to-end login. For the pilot we support both SAML and OIDC, but you mentioned SAML is preferred.
[02:20] Tom Baker: yeah SAML for enterprise SSO. question: can Redwood support Just-in-Time provisioning or do we need SCIM?
[02:29] Priya Nair: today we support SAML with user assertions and a basic SCIM sync for provisioning on Dedicated and Private deployments. for Hosted POC we can do manual mapping or a SCIM demo with a scheduled sync.
[02:44] Kenji Watanabe (joining): sorry i'm late, jumped out for a quick stand. want to make sure we cover retention windows — that's the blocker for our legal team.
[02:52] Priya Nair: good timing. Sofia, Tom — what window are you thinking? 30, 90, 365?
[03:00] Sofia Lin: engineering prefers 90 as a default for this pilot; legal asked to see 30 and 365 options and tradeoffs. storage cost is a concern.
[03:09] Aisha Rahman: also need to confirm if Redwood supports per-tenant retention policies and ability to purge on demand.
[03:17] Diego Santos: yes per-tenant retention is supported on Dedicated and Private deployments. for Hosted we provide configuration options and can trigger ad-hoc purge workflows; those do require coordination for full immutability guarantees.
[03:31] Tom Baker: and audit logs for those purge actions — we need an immutable trail. is that captured?
[03:36] Diego Santos: yes purge and retention actions are recorded; we can export audit trails as part of the SOC2 evidence pack. small caveat: for Hosted there is a slight delay in consolidation of long term logs, but we can provide a streaming export for real-time ingestion.
[03:53] Priya Nair: Diego, can you show a quick high-level latency snapshot from the pilot? just ballpark tokens per second, 95th percentile latency numbers.
[04:03] Diego Santos: sure. quick share — in our staging runs with your sample workload we saw ~120 tokens/s per GPU, 95th percentile latency for 256 tokens was about 220ms on average. again these are with quantized model variant; full precision had slightly higher latency.
[04:24] Sofia Lin: that's in the ballpark of our SLA needs. how consistent was that under burst?
[04:29] Diego Santos: under burst we saw a 10-15% tail increase; Dedicated reserved capacity reduces that significantly. we can run a targeted stress test next week to show variance.
[04:41] Priya Nair: let's do that. schedule it week of 9/28 and include your DevOps folks.
[04:48] Aisha Rahman: noted.

--- Topics: SOC2 scoping and evidence
[05:00] Priya Nair: on SOC2 — Noah, quick status on the docs we promised?
[05:06] Noah Patel: we have a condensed SOC2 scoping note and a security pack we can share. it outlines where evidence lives, sample controls, and how we map Pilot artifacts to trust services criteria.
[05:18] Tom Baker: will that include how Keystone keys are managed? we use a company KMS and want to know key custody for Hosted vs Dedicated.
[05:27] Noah Patel: yes the pack explains KMS integrations and options: customer-managed KMS for Private, KMS integration for Dedicated, and Redwood-managed KMS for Hosted by default. we'll call out what evidence we can provide for key rotation and access.
[05:41] Aisha Rahman: also need SSO audit events surfaced in our SIEM. can you push logs to Splunk or S3?
[05:49] Diego Santos: we can push to S3 and set up an S3 sink; Splunk is supported via your ingestion pipeline. we recommend S3 for handoff and then you can hook Splunk ingestion to it.
[05:59] Tom Baker: about audit log format: can you include both raw and normalized formats? makes our compliance team's life easier.
[06:07] Diego Santos: yes raw + normalized. I'll add a short README with field mappings.

--- Mid-call clarifications and micro-issues
[06:20] Sofia Lin: quick question — if we request shorter retention on production data during pilot, does that affect model caching or prompt-level KV cache?
[06:30] Diego Santos: good callout — prefix/KV cache is orthogonal to audit retention. caching may keep ephemeral tokens for latency reasons but we can configure cache TTLs to respect retention windows. for strict purge workflows we can flush caches as part of purge.
[06:47] Aisha Rahman: perfect. that addresses legal's worry.

[07:00] Kenji Watanabe: another ask — we want a short demo of how model rollbacks are handled if a quality regression is detected. not security but relevant to governance.
[07:09] Priya Nair: happy to do a quick canary/rollback demo in the next session, Diego can lead.

--- Audit log ingestion demo (high level)
[07:20] Diego Santos: OK quick run-through — ingest pipeline accepts JSON, CSV, and syslog. we map incoming fields using a mapping file; missing fields are flagged and we surface a sample row with errors. sample parsed event: {event_type: "document.query", user_id: "<redacted>", timestamp: "2026-09-18T12:34:56Z"} — note: transcription may show the object braces but real exports are newline-delimited JSON.
[08:05] Tom Baker: we need to ensure user identifiers are pseudonymized. can you show how that looks?
[08:12] Diego Santos: yes pseudonymization module replaces emails and IPs with hashed tokens; original values are not retained in the redacted export.
[08:22] Aisha Rahman: do you store any of the raw logs in Redwood-managed buckets during parsing?
[08:28] Diego Santos: by default Hosted temporarily stages raw logs for 24 hours for ingestion and rollback, but we can configure that to zero-staging for compliance. Dedicated/Private can be configured to never stage raw logs in Redwood-managed storage.

--- Questions from Horizon (brief)
[08:45] Tom Baker: Q: for evidence of purge, what format does that take?
[08:49] Noah Patel: we can provide a purge manifest: timestamped entries, user scope, retention policy id, and a signed audit record. that manifest can be exported as part of the SOC2 bundle.
[09:00] Aisha Rahman: Q: what about encryption in transit for audit exports?
[09:04] Diego Santos: TLS 1.2+ for all data in transit; we also support mTLS for dedicated endpoints and signed streaming uploads.

--- Recap & next actions
[09:20] Priya Nair: quick recap — Tom to deliver sample logs; Diego will prepare ingestion demo and mapping README; Priya to share SOC2 scoping doc and security pack; Sofia to confirm retention window; schedule stress test next week.
[09:36] Aisha Rahman: can you also include expected artifacts list for our legal team so they can close the compliance gate?
[09:42] Noah Patel: yes i'll add an artifact checklist (SOC2 items, audit logs, key management evidence, SSO event logs, retention/purge manifests).
[09:52] Kenji Watanabe: and i'll coordinate internal stakeholders for the stress test time window.
[10:00] Priya Nair: perfect. we'll send the plan and links after the call. thanks everyone.
[10:06] Tom Baker: thanks all.
[10:08] Sofia Lin: thanks.

(End of transcript)
